name: Welcome + Setup Verified
description: Personal call from the broker who settled the loan. Confirms loan is functioning correctly (direct debits, offset working, repayments as expected). Introduces POLR portal and plants the first soft FFG cross-sell seed. This is the human anchor — establishes that Fox stays in the picture post-settlement.
internal_actions: Broker calls client within first 2-4 weeks post-settlement
Confirm direct debits, offset accounts, and repayment schedules are correct
Walk client through POLR portal login and features
Log call outcome and any issues in POLR
Flag any setup issues for immediate resolution
customer_outcome: Client feels supported, knows their loan is working, and has a portal they can check anytime.
deliverables: Personal phone call from settling broker
ctas: Log into your POLR portal and check your loan summary
Save your broker's direct number

ica_variation.young_practical_motor: Keep it simple and warm. They may be first-time borrowers. Reassure them everything is set up right. Mention that Fox also helps with car finance if they need a vehicle down the track.
ica_variation.established_personal_finance: Efficient and respectful of their time. They have borrowing experience. Confirm setup, highlight POLR's tracking features, mention FFG for any personal finance needs.
ica_variation.prime_convenience_repeat: Quick and easy — they value convenience. Confirm everything is running smoothly, emphasise POLR as their one-stop dashboard. Light FFG mention for vehicle upgrades.
ica_variation.business_asset: Professional tone. Confirm loan structure is optimised for their business. Highlight POLR's ability to track both business and personal lending. Mention FFG for equipment or fleet finance.
ica_variation.prime_vehicle: Friendly and straightforward. Confirm home loan setup, introduce POLR. Mention FFG naturally — they likely already have vehicle finance awareness.

purchase_type_variation.first_home_buyer: Extra reassurance — this is likely their biggest financial commitment. Walk through repayment schedule carefully. Explain offset account benefits in simple terms. Celebrate the milestone.
purchase_type_variation.new_purchase: Confirm settlement went smoothly. If upgrading, acknowledge the move. Check that old property arrangements (if retained) are also in order.
purchase_type_variation.refinance: Confirm new rate is active and savings are flowing. Show the dollar difference from their old loan. Reinforce that Fox will keep watching rates for them.
purchase_type_variation.investor: Confirm investment loan structure (IO vs P&I), rental income offset setup, and tax-relevant features. Mention POLR's property tracking for portfolio view.
purchase_type_variation.commercial: Confirm commercial loan terms, any guarantor structures, and business account linkages. More formal tone. Mention FFG for any equipment finance needs.

client_vs_nonclient: N/A — this stage only applies to settled FHL clients.
handoff_trigger: No handoff at this stage. Cross-sell seed is planted but not actioned. If client proactively asks about car/asset finance, trigger handoff HP-005 (fhl-to-ffg-cross-sell-reactive).
compliance_notes: No financial advice can be given during this call. Stick to factual setup confirmation. Do not use words: advice, guarantee, financial hardship. If client raises hardship concerns, follow escalation protocol (refer to lender hardship team). AFSL and ACL disclaimers in any written follow-up.
example_content: Hi [Name], it's [Broker] from Fox Home Loans. Just calling to check in now that your loan has settled — I want to make sure everything is running smoothly. Are your repayments coming out as expected? Great. I've also set up your POLR portal — it's where you can see your loan details, property value, and equity anytime. I'll send you the login details after this call. And just so you know, if you ever need help with car finance or equipment loans, our team at Fox Finance Group can sort that out for you too. But no rush — we're here whenever you need us.

name: 90-Day Confidence Pack
description: Automated delivery of the first major value piece. Pulls a Cotality valuation to establish the equity baseline. Includes ICA-segmented educational modules. This touchpoint proves Fox is watching and working for them even when they haven't asked.
internal_actions: Trigger Cotality API to pull current property valuation
Calculate equity position (current value minus loan balance)
Generate ICA-segmented content module
Package into POLR notification + email with PDF attachment
Log delivery and open/click tracking
customer_outcome: Client sees their property value and equity position. Gets relevant education based on their situation. Feels Fox is proactively looking after them.
deliverables: ICA-segmented education module (PDF or POLR page)
ctas: Log into POLR to see your updated property value
Read your personalised finance guide

ica_variation.young_practical_motor: Cost-to-own module — break down what their home really costs per week (mortgage, rates, insurance, maintenance). Compare to renting. Show them they're building wealth. Simple language, no jargon.
ica_variation.established_personal_finance: Portfolio snapshot — show property value alongside any other known lending. Highlight equity growth trajectory. More sophisticated content, they can handle detail.
ica_variation.prime_convenience_repeat: Quick equity summary — how much equity they've built in 90 days. One clear number. Link to POLR for detail. Keep it brief, they want the headline.
ica_variation.business_asset: Business impact module — how property equity can support business growth (security for business lending, refinance to free up cash flow). Connect personal and business finance.
ica_variation.prime_vehicle: Simple equity update with a lifestyle angle — your home is worth X, you've built Y in equity. If you're thinking about upgrading your car, that equity could help down the track.

purchase_type_variation.first_home_buyer: Cost-to-own breakdown: weekly cost of ownership vs renting. Celebrate equity built. Explain LVR improvement. FHB-specific: show how far they've come since settlement.
purchase_type_variation.new_purchase: Property value update and equity snapshot. If they retained old property, show portfolio view. Market context for their suburb.
purchase_type_variation.refinance: Savings proof: show actual dollar savings since refinancing. Compare old vs new rate impact over 12 months. Reinforce the decision was smart.
purchase_type_variation.investor: Rental yield tracking setup. Equity position for portfolio leverage. Tax-time preparation notes. Suburb rental market data.
purchase_type_variation.commercial: Commercial property valuation update. Business equity position. Market comparison for commercial properties in their area.

client_vs_nonclient: N/A — this stage only applies to settled FHL clients.
handoff_trigger: No direct handoff trigger. If equity position reveals opportunity for asset finance (e.g., strong equity + ICA indicates vehicle need), flag for Month 9 FFG Momentum Pack targeting.
compliance_notes: Cotality valuation is an estimate, not a formal valuation — must include disclaimer. Do not state equity figures as financial advice. Disclaimer: 'This information is general in nature and does not constitute financial advice.' No use of: advice, guarantee. Property values are indicative only.
example_content:
Subject: Your 90-day property update is ready

Hi [Name],

It's been 3 months since your loan settled, and we've pulled a fresh valuation on your property.

Your property snapshot:
- Current estimated value: $[X]
- Your loan balance: $[Y]
- Equity built: $[Z]

We've also put together a [Cost-to-Own Guide / Portfolio Snapshot / Savings Report] based on your situation. You can view it in your POLR portal.

[Log in to POLR]

As always, if you have any questions, your broker [Name] is just a call away.

Fox Home Loans

*Property valuations are estimates provided by Cotality and do not constitute a formal valuation. This information is general in nature and does not constitute financial advice.*

name: Proactive Pricing Review
description: Fox proactively reviews the client's rate against current market and calls the lender to reprice WITHOUT the client asking. This is the signature Fox differentiator — proving ongoing value. If repricing is achieved, the client gets a call with the good news. If not, they still get told Fox tried.
internal_actions: Pull current rate from LMS (Finshaw's/Connective)
Compare against current lender rates and market rates
Call lender to negotiate repricing
Document outcome (repriced amount or rejection reason)
Call client with result
Update POLR with new rate if repriced
Log in CRM for compliance trail
customer_outcome: Client either gets a lower rate (saving real money) or knows Fox tried on their behalf. Either way, they feel looked after and are less likely to churn to another broker.
deliverables: Updated POLR dashboard if rate changed
ctas: Check your updated rate in POLR
Let us know if your circumstances have changed

ica_variation.young_practical_motor: Focus on the dollar saving per week/month. Make it tangible. 'We just saved you $47 a month — that's a tank of fuel every fortnight.' Simple wins.
ica_variation.established_personal_finance: Focus on the rate differential and annual savings. They appreciate the detail. Show the comparison table. Mention this is an ongoing service.
ica_variation.prime_convenience_repeat: Lead with the result, not the process. 'Good news — we got your rate down. You don't need to do anything, it's already done.' They love zero-effort value.
ica_variation.business_asset: Frame the saving in business terms. 'That's $X back in your cash flow this year.' Connect to business planning.
ica_variation.prime_vehicle: Straightforward: 'We checked your rate, negotiated with your lender, and got you a better deal. Here's what you'll save.' Keep it simple and positive.

purchase_type_variation.first_home_buyer: Celebrate any saving — it's meaningful to a FHB. Explain how repricing works (many FHBs don't know this exists). Frame Fox as their ongoing advocate.
purchase_type_variation.new_purchase: Standard repricing approach. Note any LVR improvement since purchase that strengthens the repricing argument.
purchase_type_variation.refinance: Careful messaging — they just refinanced. Focus on 'we're still watching your rate even after settling.' Shows the refinance wasn't a one-off.
purchase_type_variation.investor: Focus on yield improvement. Lower rate = better net yield on investment property. Frame in returns language.
purchase_type_variation.commercial: Commercial repricing is harder but still attempted. Focus on the margin reduction achieved and annual cash flow impact.

client_vs_nonclient: N/A — this stage only applies to settled FHL clients.
handoff_trigger: No direct handoff. However, the repricing call is a natural conversation moment. If client mentions vehicle, equipment, or asset needs during the call, broker should warm-handoff to FFG using HP-005 (fhl-to-ffg-cross-sell-reactive).
compliance_notes: Repricing is a service, not advice. Do not recommend switching lenders during this touchpoint (that's Month 15). Rate comparisons must use current published rates. Any savings projection must include disclaimer about variable rate changes. Do not use: advice, guarantee.
example_content:
Phone: 'Hi [Name], it's [Broker] from Fox Home Loans. I've got some good news — I reviewed your rate against what [Lender] is offering new customers, and there was a gap. So I called them and negotiated a better rate for you. Your rate has dropped from [X]% to [Y]%, which saves you about $[Z] a month. You don't need to do anything — it's already done. I've updated your POLR portal too, so you can see the new figures. How's everything else going?'

Follow-up email: 'Hi [Name], just confirming the rate reduction we discussed. Your new rate of [Y]% is now active. You can see the updated figures in your POLR portal. If anything changes with your situation, just let us know — we're always here.'

name: FFG Momentum Pack
description: The KEY cross-sell moment. By Month 9, the client trusts Fox, has seen value (repricing, valuations), and is primed for an FFG introduction. Five ICA-targeted packs plus an equity release pack. Content is educational and permission-based, not pushy. Positions FFG as a natural extension of the Fox relationship.
internal_actions: Select ICA-targeted pack based on client profile
Generate equity release content if equity threshold met
Package cross-sell content into email + POLR notification
Set up FFG handoff tracking
Alert FFG team of warm leads who engage
Log delivery and engagement metrics
customer_outcome: Client discovers FFG can help with their next financial need — car, equipment, personal loan — without feeling sold to. Those who engage are warm-handed to FFG.
deliverables: ICA-targeted FFG introduction pack (email + POLR content)
FFG service overview relevant to their ICA
ctas: See what Fox Finance Group can do for you
Chat with our asset finance team — no obligation
Explore using your equity for your next move

ica_variation.young_practical_motor: Car finance introduction. 'You've been building equity in your home — now let's talk about getting into the right car.' Focus on affordability, flexible terms, Fox handling everything. Mention novated leasing if employed. Tone: encouraging, simple, no pressure.
ica_variation.established_personal_finance: Personal finance options. 'With your property growing in value, there are smart ways to structure your next move.' Debt consolidation, personal loans, or refinance-to-release options. Tone: informed, strategic, respectful of their experience.
ica_variation.prime_convenience_repeat: Convenience angle. 'You already trust Fox with your home loan — why not let us handle your car finance too? One team, one portal, zero hassle.' Focus on ease and simplicity. Tone: effortless, time-saving.
ica_variation.business_asset: Business equipment and fleet finance. 'Your property equity could support your next business investment.' Equipment finance, fleet vehicles, cash flow solutions. Tone: professional, growth-focused, strategic.
ica_variation.prime_vehicle: Direct vehicle finance offer. 'Thinking about a new car? Fox Finance Group can get you a great deal — and we already know your financial picture.' Competitive rates, fast approval, seamless experience. Tone: confident, straightforward.

purchase_type_variation.first_home_buyer: FHB equity release: 'You've been building equity since day one. Here's how that equity could help you with your next goal — whether it's a car, renovations, or something else.' Educational, not aggressive.
purchase_type_variation.new_purchase: Standard ICA pack. If they upgraded from a previous property, they likely have strong equity. Frame FFG as the next logical step in their Fox relationship.
purchase_type_variation.refinance: Refinance-specific: 'You saved money by refinancing. Now let's look at other ways to optimise your finances.' Position FFG as part of the same optimisation mindset.
purchase_type_variation.investor: Investor equity release: 'Your investment property is building equity. Here's how to put that equity to work — business assets, vehicles, or further investment.' Sophisticated, returns-focused.
purchase_type_variation.commercial: Commercial equity release: 'Your commercial property equity could fund your next equipment purchase or fleet expansion — without touching your cash flow.' Business-focused, practical.

client_vs_nonclient: N/A — this stage only applies to settled FHL clients. Non-clients would receive a different conversion-focused touchpoint.
handoff_trigger: YES. If client engages (opens email, clicks CTA, logs into POLR to view FFG content), trigger HP-004 (fhl-to-ffg-cross-sell-proactive). Warm lead data passes to FFG team (Sam Drew or assigned broker). Client is NOT handed off without engagement signal.
compliance_notes: Cross-sell content must not constitute financial advice. No guarantees about FFG approval or rates. Equity release content must note that accessing equity increases total debt and repayments. Disclaimer: 'This is general information only and does not constitute financial advice. Any finance application is subject to lender approval and terms.' Do not use: advice, guarantee, financial hardship.
both_settled_override: If client is already settled with BOTH FFG and FHL, this touchpoint transforms from cross-sell to relationship deepening. Instead of introducing FFG, deliver a 'Your Fox Finance Portfolio' summary showing both loans, combined equity, and next opportunities. No cross-sell CTA needed — focus on retention and satisfaction.
example_content:
Subject: Your home equity could open new doors

Hi [Name],

It's been 9 months since your home loan settled, and your property has been building value. Here's where you stand:

- Estimated property value: $[X]
- Current loan balance: $[Y]
- Available equity: $[Z]

Did you know Fox Finance Group — the other side of our business — helps people just like you with [car finance / equipment loans / personal finance]?

We've put together a short guide based on your situation: [ICA-specific pack name]

[View your guide in POLR]

No pressure, no obligation. Just good information from a team that already knows your financial picture.

Fox Home Loans

*This is general information only and does not constitute financial advice. Any finance application is subject to lender approval and terms.*

name: Annual Property & Loan Strategy Review
description: The signature annual review. Comprehensive assessment of property value movement, equity built over 12 months, loan performance, and forward strategy options. This is the most substantial touchpoint in the lifecycle. Broker-led call backed by automated data preparation.
internal_actions: Pull fresh Cotality valuation
Calculate 12-month equity growth
Review rate competitiveness
Prepare annual review document in POLR
Broker schedules and conducts review call
Document strategy discussion and client goals
Update POLR with review outcomes
customer_outcome: Client gets a clear picture of their 12-month progress. Understands their options. Feels like they have a financial partner, not just a broker who settled a loan.
ctas: Book your annual review call with [Broker]
View your 12-month summary in POLR

ica_variation.young_practical_motor: Celebrate their first year of home ownership. Show equity growth in simple terms. Introduce concepts like offset strategies or extra repayments. Keep it encouraging.
ica_variation.established_personal_finance: Detailed portfolio review. Compare property performance against broader market. Discuss strategic options — investment property, refinance, equity release. They want substance.
ica_variation.prime_convenience_repeat: Quick headline summary with a 5-minute call option. 'Here's your year in review: property up X%, equity at $Y, rate still competitive. Anything you want to chat about?' Respect their time.
ica_variation.business_asset: Frame the review in business context. How does property equity support business plans for the coming year? Equipment needs? Expansion? Cash flow?
ica_variation.prime_vehicle: Straightforward review. Property doing well? Rate still good? Any upcoming needs? Direct and practical.

purchase_type_variation.first_home_buyer: First anniversary of ownership. Show LVR improvement, equity built, and what doors that equity opens. Introduce the concept of next steps (renovate, invest, upgrade) without pushing.
purchase_type_variation.new_purchase: 12-month value assessment. If retained old property, show portfolio performance. Discuss whether current structure is still optimal.
purchase_type_variation.refinance: 12-month savings report: total saved since refinancing. Compare current rate against market. Discuss whether a further refinance makes sense in another 6-12 months.
purchase_type_variation.investor: Investment performance review. Rental yield, equity growth, portfolio leverage position. Discuss strategy for Year 2 — hold, add, restructure.
purchase_type_variation.commercial: Commercial property performance. Valuation movement, loan structure review. Discuss business plans that may affect property strategy.

client_vs_nonclient: N/A — this stage only applies to settled FHL clients.
handoff_trigger: If annual review conversation reveals asset finance needs (vehicle replacement, equipment, personal loan), broker warm-handoffs to FFG using HP-005 (fhl-to-ffg-cross-sell-reactive). If client expresses interest in investment property, broker handles directly within FHL.
compliance_notes: Annual review must not constitute financial advice. Strategy options are general in nature. Property valuations are estimates. If recommending structural changes (e.g., switch to IO, refinance), client must be referred through proper application process. Disclaimer on all written materials. Do not use: advice, guarantee, financial hardship.
example_content:
Phone: 'Hi [Name], it's [Broker] from Fox Home Loans. It's been 12 months since your loan settled, so I've put together your annual review. Your property has moved from $[original] to $[current], which means you've built about $[equity] in equity this year. Your rate is still competitive at [X]%, and I'll be doing another repricing check at the 18-month mark. I've loaded all the detail into your POLR portal. Are there any goals for the year ahead I should know about?'

Follow-up email: 'Hi [Name], great chatting today. Your annual review is now in your POLR portal — [link]. Summary: property value $[X], equity $[Y], rate [Z]%. Let me know if you'd like to explore any of the options we discussed.'

name: Refinance Pathway
description: Present three clear pathways based on the client's situation and goals. Educational content that shows the pros and cons of each path with real numbers from their loan. Not pushing refinance — presenting informed options.
internal_actions: Calculate current equity and LVR
Model three scenarios with real numbers
Generate personalised pathway document
Deliver via email + POLR notification
Track engagement for broker follow-up
customer_outcome: Client understands their options with real numbers. Feels empowered to make a decision (or not). Knows Fox is there when they're ready.
deliverables: POLR portal update with interactive calculator
ctas: Explore your three pathways in POLR
Book a call to discuss which path suits you

three_pathways.path_1_pay_down: Accelerate repayments. Show impact of extra $100/week. Time saved. Interest saved. Best for: clients who want to be mortgage-free faster.
three_pathways.path_2_invest: Use equity to invest. Show borrowing capacity for investment property. Rental yield offset. Portfolio growth. Best for: clients ready to build wealth.
three_pathways.path_3_refinance: Switch lenders for better deal. Show potential savings. Compare current vs best available. Factor in switching costs. Best for: clients on uncompetitive rates.

ica_variation.young_practical_motor: Focus on Path 1 (pay down) and Path 3 (refinance for better rate). Investment is likely premature. Use simple comparisons: 'An extra $50 a week could save you $X over the life of your loan.'
ica_variation.established_personal_finance: Present all three paths with detail. They can handle sophisticated modelling. Include tax implications for investment path. They may already be thinking about this.
ica_variation.prime_convenience_repeat: Lead with whichever path requires least effort. If rate is uncompetitive, lead with Path 3 and emphasise Fox handles everything. If rate is fine, lead with 'you're in a good spot.'
ica_variation.business_asset: Frame Path 2 in business terms — equity release for business investment, not just property investment. Path 1 for cash flow improvement. Path 3 if rate is poor.
ica_variation.prime_vehicle: Keep it practical. Show each path in monthly dollar terms. Which path frees up the most cash? Which builds the most wealth? Let them decide.

purchase_type_variation.first_home_buyer: Path 1 emphasis — most FHBs want to build equity faster. Path 2 introduction for those who are ready. Path 3 if their rate has drifted.
purchase_type_variation.new_purchase: All three paths equally relevant. Tailor based on whether they retained old property (if so, portfolio view).
purchase_type_variation.refinance: Sensitive — they already refinanced 15 months ago. Frame as 'checking in, not suggesting you switch again.' Path 1 and Path 2 more appropriate unless rate gap is significant.
purchase_type_variation.investor: Path 2 emphasis — they're already investors. Show how equity unlocks next property. Path 1 less relevant. Path 3 if rate is poor.
purchase_type_variation.commercial: Business-focused variants of each path. Path 2 = business expansion. Path 1 = reduce business debt exposure. Path 3 = optimise commercial rate.

client_vs_nonclient: N/A — this stage only applies to settled FHL clients.
handoff_trigger: If client engages with Path 2 (invest) or Path 3 (refinance), trigger broker follow-up call. If Path 2 engagement includes interest in asset-backed investment, flag for FFG cross-sell via HP-004.
compliance_notes: This content must be clearly labelled as general information, not personal financial advice. Scenario modelling uses assumptions that must be disclosed. Investment pathway must include risk warnings. Refinance pathway must note switching costs and break fees. Do not use: advice, guarantee, financial hardship. Include disclaimer: 'These scenarios are illustrative only and based on current rates and assumptions. They do not constitute financial advice.'
example_content:
Subject: Three paths forward for your home loan

Hi [Name],

You're 15 months into your home loan, and your position has strengthened. Here's a quick look at three paths you could take from here:

1. Pay down faster — An extra $[X]/week could save you $[Y] in interest and cut [Z] years off your loan.
2. Use your equity — With $[equity] in equity, you could explore investment options that put your property to work.
3. Refinance — Current market rates suggest you could save $[savings]/month by switching. We'd handle everything.

Each path has pros and cons, and there's no rush. We've loaded a detailed comparison into your POLR portal.

[View your pathways in POLR]

Want to talk it through? Book a call with [Broker] — [booking link].

Fox Home Loans

*These scenarios are illustrative only and based on current rates and assumptions. They do not constitute financial advice.*

name: Action Window
description: Trigger-based touchpoint. Scans for actionable events: fixed rate expiry, significant market rate movement, client goal changes logged in POLR, or lender advantage opportunities. Only fires when there's a real reason to act. If no trigger exists, a light check-in is sent instead.
internal_actions: Scan for trigger events (fixed expiry, rate movement, goal change, lender offer)
If trigger found: generate action-specific communication
If no trigger: send light 18-month check-in
Broker review of any recommended actions
Deliver via email + POLR + broker call if action required
customer_outcome: Client receives timely, relevant action prompts when something actually matters. No spam. No unnecessary contact. When Fox reaches out at 18 months, it's because there's a reason.
deliverables: Updated POLR dashboard with action recommendation
Broker call if action involves structural change
ctas: Your fixed rate expires in [X] weeks — let's plan your next move
Rates have dropped — see what this means for you
Your goals have changed — let's update your strategy

trigger_types.fixed_rate_expiry: Fixed rate ending within 60 days. Present options: refix, switch to variable, refinance. Include comparison of each option.
trigger_types.market_rate_movement: Significant rate drop (>0.25%) since last review. Show impact on their loan. Offer repricing or refinance assessment.
trigger_types.client_goal_change: Client updated goals in POLR (e.g., planning to sell, wanting to invest, life change). Trigger strategy conversation.
trigger_types.lender_advantage: Their lender is offering better deals to new customers. Trigger repricing attempt or refinance discussion.
trigger_types.no_trigger: Light check-in: 'It's been 18 months. Everything is tracking well. Here's a quick update on your position. We're here if anything changes.'

ica_variation.young_practical_motor: Simple and action-oriented. 'Your fixed rate is ending soon — here are your options in plain English.' Guide them through the decision.
ica_variation.established_personal_finance: Detailed analysis of the trigger and implications. They want to understand the 'why' behind any recommendation.
ica_variation.prime_convenience_repeat: 'We spotted something that needs your attention. Here's what we recommend, and we can handle it all for you.' Minimal effort required.
ica_variation.business_asset: Frame trigger in business impact terms. 'This rate change affects your cash flow by $X/month. Here are your options.'
ica_variation.prime_vehicle: Practical and direct. 'Something's changed with your loan situation. Here's what it means and what we can do.'

purchase_type_variation.first_home_buyer: Extra guidance on what fixed rate expiry means and why it matters. Many FHBs won't understand the implications without explanation.
purchase_type_variation.new_purchase: Standard trigger response. Factor in whether they have multiple properties.
purchase_type_variation.refinance: Tread carefully — they may not want to hear about refinancing again. Focus on repricing first, refinance only if significant gap.
purchase_type_variation.investor: Investment-focused analysis. How does the trigger affect yield, cash flow, tax position?
purchase_type_variation.commercial: Commercial rate triggers. Factor in business lending cycle and cash flow implications.

client_vs_nonclient: N/A — this stage only applies to settled FHL clients.
handoff_trigger: If action window conversation reveals asset finance needs, trigger HP-005 (fhl-to-ffg-cross-sell-reactive). If refinance is recommended, this re-enters the FHL pipeline as a new application via EP-003 (fhl-refinance-return). The lifecycle resets from Month 1 after new settlement.
compliance_notes: Any recommendation to switch rates or lenders must go through proper application process. This touchpoint is informational — actual changes require formal engagement. Fixed rate expiry notifications must include comparison of options without recommending one. Do not use: advice, guarantee, financial hardship.
lifecycle_reset_note: After Month 18, the lifecycle either resets (if refinance/new application occurs) or transitions to ongoing low-frequency nurture with annual reviews and trigger-based outreach.
example_content:
Subject: Heads up — your fixed rate expires in 8 weeks

Hi [Name],

Your fixed rate of [X]% expires on [date]. After that, your loan will revert to the variable rate of [Y]%, which changes your repayment from $[current] to approximately $[new].

Here are your three options:

1. Refix — Lock in a new fixed rate. Current best: [rate]% for [term].
2. Go variable — More flexibility, current variable rate: [rate]%.
3. Refinance — We can check if another lender offers a better deal. Current best market rate: [rate]%.

We recommend [no specific recommendation — just the options]. Want to chat it through? Book a call with [Broker]: [link].

Fox Home Loans

*This information is general in nature and does not constitute financial advice.*

name: Welcome + Setup Verified
description: Light welcome touchpoint. Confirms finance is in place, vehicle/asset delivered, and repayments are set up correctly. Introduces POLR portal. Plants soft FHL seed for those who don't already have a home loan with Fox.
internal_actions: Broker or admin calls within 2-4 weeks of settlement
Confirm asset delivery and finance setup
Walk through POLR portal access
Check for FHL relationship flag
Log call outcome
customer_outcome: Client knows their finance is working and they have a portal to track it. First impression of ongoing Fox care.
ctas: Log into POLR to see your loan summary
Save your broker's direct number

ica_variation.young_practical_motor: Excited about their new car. Keep it celebratory and simple. 'Congrats on the new ride! Let's make sure everything is set up right.' Soft mention: 'If you ever need help with a home loan, we do that too.'
ica_variation.established_personal_finance: Efficient check-in. Confirm setup, introduce POLR, mention FHL briefly. They may already have a mortgage elsewhere.
ica_variation.prime_convenience_repeat: Quick and easy. 'Everything's sorted. Here's your portal. We'll check in again at 3 months.' Minimal friction.
ica_variation.business_asset: Professional tone. Confirm equipment/fleet finance setup. Discuss any tax or structure considerations. Mention FHL for commercial property needs.
ica_variation.prime_vehicle: Straightforward car finance confirmation. Happy energy. 'Your loan is all set up. Enjoy the new car. We're here if you need anything.'

purchase_type_variation: N/A — FFG does not have FHL Purchase Type variations. ICA variation covers messaging differences.
client_vs_nonclient: N/A — this stage only applies to settled FFG clients.
